sources.title: 2020 U.S. Religion Census: Religious Congregations & Adherents Study
sources.provider: Association of Statisticians of American Religious Bodies (ASARB)
sources.dataset_version: 2020 summary and group detail workbooks (files updated 2023-06-23 per the landing page)
sources.license: Workbooks carry 'Copyright (c) 2022 by the Association of Statisticians of American Religious Bodies (ASARB). All rights reserved' and a suggested citation. The landing page offers them as free downloads and states no further terms of use; the ARDA archives the same study with a DOI and citation. Only per-county Catholic Church counts and ratios derived from them are republished here, with the citation.
sources.citation: Clifford Grammich, Erica Dollhopf, Mary Gautier, Richard Houseal, Dale E. Jones, Alexei Krindatch, Richie Stanley, and Scott Thumma. 2022. 2020 U.S. Religion Census: Religious Congregations & Adherents Study. Association of Statisticians of American Religious Bodies. County file archived at the ARDA: DOI 10.17605/OSF.IO/ET2A5.
sources.notes: Catholic Church = group code 081. Adherents are all ages and include people the Church counts as members; they are not Mass attendees and not women 20-29. Connecticut is reported by its eight former counties, which do not match the planning regions ACS 2024 uses. Puerto Rico is not covered.

sources.notes: EU/EFTA reporting countries only. Status codes (p provisional, e estimated, b break in series, i imputed) kept per value. Divorces in the year per 1,000 average population (all ages).
